slides.title: Lock it up
slides.text: At home you lock the door and keep the key safe. Online you do the same: lock it, keep the key, keep a spare copy.
slides.alt: The mailbox key builder: pick words for a passphrase, the key that locks your mailbox in Packet Post.

slides.title: Private or fine to share?
slides.text: Some things are private: where you live, your birthday, your passphrase. Fun things, like your favorite animal or a joke you made up, are fine to share.
slides.alt: The sharing sort: cards to split into Share and Keep Private, from favorite animals to passphrases.

slides.title: Build a passphrase
slides.text: Pick four random words that do not belong together. It is long, so it is hard to guess. The funny picture makes it easy to remember.
slides.alt: The passphrase is taking shape: words are being picked for the mailbox key, and longer means harder to guess.

slides.title: Who may know it?
slides.text: Keep your passphrase secret, even from your best friend. Only a parent or another trusted adult may know it.
slides.alt: Okay to Tell: a sorting round about who may hear what, where a passphrase is never fine to share.

slides.title: Keep a spare copy
slides.text: A backup is a spare copy kept somewhere else. If the tablet breaks, your photos are still safe.
slides.alt: A Good Spare Copy: the sorting round that tells a real backup, kept somewhere else, from a copy that is not.

words.means: only for you and the trusted adults who look after you
a secret key made of several random words
a spare copy kept in another place

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Packet Post at Lock It and finish all 6 levels. In the game your passphrase is called your mailbox key. You only tap tiles, so nothing real gets shared.
slides.alt: The mailbox key builder: pick words for a passphrase, the key that locks your mailbox in Packet Post.
